crop.description:
The part of the view to show (a page): "x0,y0,x1,y1" in model
millimetres of the view's frame -- a plan's is the model's x and y, a
section's the cut plane's own -- the page fitted to it and nothing
outside it drawn. Empty shows the whole view.

dimensions.description:
"auto" (the default) figures the overall sizes; "none" draws no
dimensions.

hidden.description:
What to do with edges the solid hides: "dashed" (the default), "omit" or
"solid".

labels.description:
Notes at points of the model (a page), each "x,y,z=text" with the
point in model millimetres: written centred on where the point lands,
on a white ground.

layers.description:
Display layers, as `Render` takes them: `envelope=off` hides a
layer, `labels=on` shows one the script declared hidden. A page
draws only what these leave visible.

items.description:
A display-layer override for one render: the layer by name and
what to change about it. A field left unset keeps the layer's own default
from `layer(...)`. The empty name is the implicit layer of untagged bodies
(`cadpole render --layer other=off`, unless the script declares a layer
called `other`).

opacity.description:
Draw them at this opacity, 0..1: below 1 they are ghosted, translucent
the way `material(opacity=)` is, on every backend.

visible.description: Draw the layer's bodies at all.

legend.description: Legend swatches (a page), each "#rrggbb=what it means", in order.

look.description:
A page of one view, when this or `section` is set: "color"
(the default) draws what `Render` with a section shows, as vectors --
every surface the eye sees filled in its body's colour, nearer over
farther, edges as fine lines, the cut faces filled in the colour of
what they cut and outlined, and labels the script made with
`extrude(text(...))` written as text the size they are in the model;
"lines" draws the same view as drafting: the cut hatched, what lies
beyond as hidden-line-removed strokes. Then the title, `subtitle`,
`legend`, a scale bar, a north arrow on a plan, `labels` and `note`
around it, every word real text a PDF reader can select. On a page,
`view` is a direction to look from ("top", the default, or "front",
"north", ...) and `section` the cut; `dimensions` and `hidden` do not
apply. With neither field set the drawing is the one `view` alone
names, as before.

model_unit.description:
What one unit of the script is (a page): "mm" (the default),
"cm", "m", "in" or "ft". A script drawn one unit to the foot is scaled
to millimetres once, here, as `cadpole bake --model-unit` scales it,
so the scale, the scale bar and the label sizes are true; `section`,
`crop` and `labels` are then in the script's units too, and with "ft"
or "in" the page writes feet and inches unless `units` says otherwise.

north_degrees.description:
Where north is, in degrees clockwise from +y seen from above, for a
plan's north arrow (a page); 0 defers to the document's
`render_defaults(north=)`, else +y is north.

note.description: A footnote along the bottom of the page.
examples: North up; the street at the bottom

param_overrides.description: Parameter overrides, as `name=value`, exactly as `Render` takes them.

scale.description:
Drawing scale, as "1:2", "2:1" or the architectural form
(a quarter inch to the foot). Empty fits the model to the sheet and snaps
to a standard ratio.

section.description:
The page's cut, written the way `Render` takes it: "z=1700"
removes everything above z = 1700 and looks down at what is left (a
floor plan); "x=26" removes everything beyond x = 26 and looks toward -x
at the cut; "-x=26" keeps that side instead; "y=" likewise. The value
is model millimetres or any written length ("5'-6\""). Empty draws the
whole model from `view`: a roof plan, an elevation.

subtitle.description: A line under the title (a page).

title.description:
Title-block title. The scale, and the document name as the project, are
filled in for you.

tolerance.description:
Tessellation tolerance in mm (0 = engine default). Finer means smoother
curves in the drawing and a slower export.

units.description:
How lengths are written: "mm" (the default), "cm", "m", "in", "ft" or
"ft-in" for the architectural feet-and-inches form.

view.description:
What to draw. "three-view" (the default) lays out front, top and right
plus an isometric on one sheet. A single view name - "front", "back",
"top", "bottom", "left", "right", "iso" - draws just that one.
"section:z=40" (or x=/y=) cuts the model with a plane at that coordinate
and hatches the cut face; the coordinate is millimetres, or any written
length ("1.5in", "12'-6\"", "3.65 m"). "sheet:A2.0" is the sheet numbered
A2.0 of the script's own sheet_set(), title block and all, and "sheets"
every sheet of it as one PDF; of the other fields only `format`,
`tolerance` and the parameters apply to a sheet.

title: Draw a document as a dimensioned 2D drawing
